extraction.summary: Ahmed, Dodelson, Greene and Sorkin combine the causal-set picture of Poisson fluctuations in spacetime volume with the unimodular-gravity conjugacy of Lambda and four-volume. They infer a heuristic fluctuation scale Delta Lambda ~ 1/sqrt(V), assume a zero target mean, choose the past light-cone four-volume, and implement Lambda as a random walk in action per element. Their illustrative homogeneous cosmology keeps the Friedmann equation while dropping the acceleration equation. Some selected histories have a late positive Lambda-like contribution, but the simulations also expose a tension between fluctuation amplitude and histories terminated when total density becomes negative. The paper explicitly leaves the full quantum dynamics, conservation-compatible evolution and behavior through nonpositive total density unresolved. No data likelihood is fit and no parameter-free prediction of the observed Lambda is obtained.

ideas.title: Causal-set volume fluctuations motivate a declining Lambda fluctuation scale
ideas.description: The authors combine a discrete element count N identified macroscopically with four-volume V, Poisson count fluctuations of scale sqrt(N), and the unimodular-gravity conjugacy of Lambda and V to motivate Delta Lambda ~ 1/sqrt(V). They then take the target mean to be zero as an assumption whose mechanism remains unknown. The paper says a quantum dynamics for causal sets is not yet available; this is a heuristic magnitude argument, not a derived stochastic law or a derivation of the measured value.
locators: PDF p. 2, Section II and Eq. (1)
PDF p. 3, Eq. (2) and surrounding text

equations.conventions_definitions: V is four-volume; the preceding argument identifies Poisson fluctuations in element number N with Delta V ~ sqrt(V), and treats Lambda as conjugate to V.
equations.domain: Heuristic causal-set/unimodular argument; the zero mean or target value is separately assumed, not derived.
equations.confidence: High for transcription; the paper expressly leaves the underlying quantum dynamics and interpretation open.

equations.conventions_definitions: The authors approximate V by the fourth power of the Hubble radius and set 8 pi G = 1; rho_Lambda denotes the cosmological-term energy-density scale in these units.
equations.domain: Order-of-magnitude scaling, asserted for all epochs under the chosen volume interpretation.
equations.confidence: High for transcription; the V-to-H estimate and target mean are modeling assumptions.

ideas.title: The fluctuation-controlling volume is chosen as a representative past light cone
ideas.description: For an observation-oriented implementation, the paper identifies V(t) with the four-volume of the backward light cone of a representative point. The authors acknowledge that this differs somewhat from the fixed-four-volume interpretation used in the unimodular path-integral motivation. They note that the light-cone volume is dominated by recent history and claim V ~ H^-4 recently even if the early universe inflated.

equations.expression: V(t) = (4 pi/3) integral_0^t dt' a(t')^3 [integral_(t')^t dt''/a(t'')]^3
equations.conventions_definitions: a(t) is the scale factor and t is proper cosmic time; the inner integral is the comoving radial distance to the past light cone.
equations.domain: Homogeneous isotropic background with a Big Bang lower limit in the paper's flat cosmological setup.
equations.confidence: High; the expression was checked in the original rendered equation.

ideas.title: Lambda is implemented as a random walk in action per causet element
ideas.description: The authors treat Lambda(N)=S(N)/N, where S is the sum of zero-mean, unit-standard-deviation random increments, and use a dimensionless alpha to set the increment amplitude. Their discrete rule uses the increase in the chosen four-volume as delta N. This is a simulation prescription motivated by the heuristic scaling; the authors do not identify it as the completed quantum causal-set law or derive alpha from fundamental parameters.

equations.conventions_definitions: N tracks the chosen four-volume in fundamental units; i indexes successive simulation time steps.

equations.expression: rho_Lambda,i+1 = [S_i + alpha xi_(i+1) sqrt(delta N_i)]/[N_i+delta N_i]
equations.conventions_definitions: xi has mean zero and standard deviation one; S_0 is set to zero at an unspecified very early t_0; alpha is an unknown dimensionless parameter.
equations.domain: Stochastic ansatz for the authors' simulation; no unique probability law beyond the stated increment moments is established in the text.
equations.confidence: High for equation and stated inputs; no inference about an unreported random-number distribution.

ideas.title: The simulation evolves with the Friedmann equation alone
ideas.description: The authors impose homogeneity and keep the first-order Friedmann equation while dropping the acceleration equation, because a time-dependent Lambda is incompatible with both equations if other stress-energy components are separately conserved. This is an acknowledged incompleteness: it does not provide a full Einstein-equation or Bianchi-consistent dynamics for fluctuating Lambda. The Bianchi/conservation issue is explicitly discussed in Section IV and is not a newly inferred objection.
locators: PDF p. 3, paragraph choosing the evolution equation

equations.conventions_definitions: Spatially flat homogeneous background; hbar=c=m_p=1 and 8 pi G=1. The text treats ordinary matter and radiation as separately conserved while Lambda varies.
equations.domain: The simulation prescription only; the independent acceleration equation is dropped.
equations.confidence: High; visually checked in the original PDF.

ideas.title: Selected random histories can mimic late-time dark energy in the chosen background prescription
ideas.description: Figure 2 shows one alpha=0.01 history in which |rho_Lambda| tracks radiation roughly as a^-4 and matter roughly as a^-3. In a different alpha=0.02 realization, the authors report Omega_Lambda fluctuating about zero with amplitude of order 0.5, positive and above one half today, and changing little back to z=1 (a=0.5). They say roughly half the realizations have positive rho_Lambda today. These are conditional model illustrations, not measured values, likelihood constraints or a posterior probability for the real universe.
locators: PDF p. 5, Fig. 2 and surrounding text
PDF pp. 5-6, Fig. 3 and surrounding text

ideas.title: Larger fluctuations raise the chance of negative total density and terminate runs
ideas.description: The authors terminate a run whenever rho_tot in Eq. (6) becomes negative. For runs started at a=10^-32, they report only about a one-in-three chance of completing at alpha=0.02. Lowering alpha to 0.01 makes such terminations rare, but a histogram of 6000 alpha=0.01 realizations rarely reaches final Omega_Lambda values they considered large enough for observations. Their stated alpha range 0.01-0.02 is a compromise in this particular implementation, not a derived or uniquely selected physical parameter range.
locators: PDF p. 6, discussion of termination and alpha choices
PDF p. 7, Fig. 4 caption and histogram

ideas.title: Conservation completions and evolution through nonpositive total density remain proposals
ideas.description: Section IV considers, but does not implement, a positive-semidefinite Lambda option and an energy-transfer option. For gravitational waves treated as radiation, the latter gives rho_dot_grav=-4 H rho_grav-Lambda_dot; generic increasing fluctuations can make rho_grav negative, while the authors say a monotonically decreasing Lambda could avoid that specific issue. They then use a classical negative-constant example to motivate possible recollapse and speculate that a fluctuating Lambda might permit recollapse reversal or that rho_tot<0 corresponds to tunneling in a fuller sum-over-histories theory. They explicitly state these behaviors do not follow from their simple ansatz and await further dynamics.
locators: PDF pp. 7-8, Section IV, Eq. (8) and following discussion

equations.conventions_definitions: The proposed example transfers energy between a radiation-like gravitational-wave component and the cosmological term; the other matter components remain separately conserved. Units set 8 pi G=1.
equations.domain: An alternative conservation completion discussed by the authors, not the evolution used in their simulations.
equations.confidence: High for transcription; the completion is proposed rather than established.

ideas.title: The authors identify possible early-universe tests but do not calculate them
ideas.description: The paper points to possible effects on primordial perturbations, BBN light-element production, CMB acoustic oscillations and later structure growth. It gives a qualitative argument about positive or negative rho_Lambda and helium abundance, but supplies no BBN likelihood, CMB spectrum, perturbation closure, structure calculation or observational fit. These are future test avenues only.

assumptions: Causal-set element count corresponds to spacetime volume with Poisson fluctuations, and Lambda is conjugate to four-volume in the relevant unimodular formulation.
The target mean of Lambda is zero; the paper assumes this and says its mechanism remains to be explained.
The volume governing fluctuations is a representative past light cone, although the authors acknowledge a tension with the fixed-volume meaning in their unimodular motivation.
The time-dependent homogeneous background keeps only the Friedmann equation and separately conserves ordinary matter/radiation; the acceleration equation is dropped.
The simulation uses a random walk with zero-mean, unit-standard-deviation increments and a free dimensionless amplitude alpha; no full quantum stochastic law or alpha derivation is provided.
A simulation is terminated if its total effective density becomes negative; no completed dynamics through that boundary is supplied.
caveats: The paper describes the causal-set quantum dynamics as undeveloped; the predicted fluctuation magnitude and zero target mean are motivational assumptions, not consequences of a completed quantum theory.
The displayed scaling rho_Lambda ~ rho_critical does not determine the observed Lambda's sign, realization, probability conditioned on survival, or detailed time correlations.

Keeping the Friedmann equation while dropping the acceleration equation is an explicit modeling choice. The paper acknowledges the contracted Bianchi identity and energy-conservation problem; it does not provide a complete field-equation closure.

The alpha compromise is entangled with the negative-density termination rule. Survival-conditioned histories and illustrative favorable realizations do not by themselves establish the probability of an observationally viable universe under a complete model.

Section IV's positive-only Lambda and energy-transfer cases are alternatives the authors discuss, not dynamics derived or implemented for the random-walk model. Recollapse, reversal and tunneling are speculative extensions and explicitly do not follow from the paper's simple ansatz.

No perturbation theory, CMB computation, structure-growth calculation, BBN calculation, observational likelihood or independent numerical reproduction is provided. The BBN discussion is qualitative and refers to source-era disagreement.
The title-page typeset date and PDF creation metadata are in 2018 while the arXiv watermark and pinned metadata say September 2002; no explanation is established.
extraction.strongest_reason: The paper makes its assumptions unusually testable: the heuristic volume-fluctuation scaling is translated into a concrete past-light-cone volume and discrete stochastic rule, and its simulations expose a specific tension between the chosen fluctuation amplitude and histories that hit negative total density. This gives later source review a clear target while keeping the numerical illustrations separate from evidence for the mechanism.
extraction.strongest_objection: The stochastic law and its zero target mean are not derived from a completed causal-set quantum dynamics, and the background prescription is not a complete conservation-consistent cosmology: the authors keep the Friedmann equation and drop the acceleration equation, while unresolved negative-total-density histories terminate. Consequently, successful example histories do not establish a viable full cosmology or a parameter-free explanation of observed Lambda. The Bianchi/conservation issue is explicitly acknowledged by the authors.
extraction.cheapest_informative_next_source_check: Check the original source cited as PDF reference [7], especially the printed arXiv item gr-qc/9706002 (version not printed), for the precise status and domain of the older 1/sqrt(V) fluctuation argument. This single cited-source check can distinguish an established result from the heuristic attribution in this paper; it would not resolve the separate Friedmann-only conservation closure.

usefulness.assessment: Useful as a foundation and source-development target for everpresent-Lambda work. It supplies an explicit heuristic chain, a volume convention, a stochastic simulation ansatz, early-universe test proposals, and candidly stated incompleteness. It is not a complete quantum-gravity derivation, a fitted model, an observational result or a scientific qualification.
usefulness.best_follow_up: A bounded source review should first check reference [7] against the claimed fluctuation scaling, while a separate equation review should keep the authors' random-walk ansatz distinct from the unimplemented conservation completions. No numerical test is authorized or needed for this Luna extraction.
usefulness.promotion_status: No idea, graph edge, prospect or design is accepted by this Luna extraction. Sol review and separate physical, consumer and qualification gates remain outstanding.
